description: A 38-pin ESP32 development board with an ESP32-WROOM-32E module, a CP2102N USB-UART bridge and a 3.3 V regulator.
summary: The board runs the user's sketch in the iynk interpreter. Pins, PWM, I2C, serial and timing follow the esp32-devkitc board profile. It is not the ESP32 chip.

models.1: Arduino-C++ subset run by the interpreter with the ESP32-DevKitC pin map.
models.2: Digital I/O on the GPIO pins the board exposes, PWM and interrupts on every output-capable pin.
models.3: 12-bit analog reads against 3.3 V, I2C master on GPIO21 and GPIO22, serial output, and the BOOT button on GPIO0.

not.1: The two Xtensa cores and FreeRTOS tasks.
not.2: Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and flash behaviour. The request stub for web-server lessons is not a radio.
not.3: The strapping-pin traps such as GPIO12 high at reset.
not.4: The 3.3 V regulator limits and the USB-UART bridge.

gap: The board has no user LED and no LED_BUILTIN: the starter wires an external LED and resistor to GPIO23. GPIO34 to GPIO39 are inputs only, and ADC2 pins cannot be read while Wi-Fi is on. No electrical ratings are listed yet, so no pin-overload check exists for this board.
